comparisons.peer_topic: Capital and RWA Changes at Year-End 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, CET1 capital increased to $201.1 billion, Tier 1 capital rose $135 million, and Total capital under Standardized approach increased $4.0 billion, while RWA grew $44.5 billion to $1,696 billion driven by client and lending activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America reported their CET1 capital amounts and ratios for the end of 2024, but JPMorgan reported significantly higher absolute CET1 capital ($275.5 billion vs $201.1 billion) and higher ratios (15.7% Standardized vs Bank of America's implied lower ratio given the $201.1B capital against $1,696B RWA results in an approx 11.9% ratio, though BAC text focuses on the absolute increase). Both firms cited earnings as a primary driver for CET1 capital increases, while JPMorgan also noted a specific SLR of 6.1% compared to BAC's supplementary leverage exposure increase.

sentences.text: • CET1 capital was $275.5 billion, and the Standardized and Advanced CET1 ratios were 15.7% and 15.8%, respectively.
At December 31, 2024, CET1 capital was $201.1 billion, an increase of $6.2 billion from December 31, 2023, primarily due to earnings, partially offset by capital distributions.

RWA under the Standardized approach, which yielded the lower CET1 capital ratio at December 31, 2024, increased $44.5 billion during 2024 to $1,696 billion primarily driven by client activity in Global Markets and lending activity in GWIM, Global Banking and Consumer Banking.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup's CET1 Capital ratio increased to 13.6% as of December 31, 2024, from 13.4% in 2023, driven by net income and a decrease in risk-weighted assets, partially offset by dividends, share repurchases, and AOCI movements.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citigroup disclosed their CET1 capital ratios for 2024 under the Standardized Approach. JPMorgan's Standardized CET1 ratio was 15.7%, which was higher than Citigroup's 13.6%. Both companies reported an increase in their CET1 ratios from the prior year (JPMorgan from 15.0% to 15.7%; Citigroup from 13.4% to 13.6%). Citigroup explicitly attributed its increase to net income and a decrease in risk-weighted assets, whereas JPMorgan's summary focuses on the final metrics without detailing the drivers in the selected sentences.

sentences.text: • CET1 capital was $275.5 billion, and the Standardized and Advanced CET1 ratios were 15.7% and 15.8%, respectively.
Citigroup's CET1 Capital ratio was 13.6% as of December 31, 2024, compared to 13.4% as of December 31, 2023, based on the Basel III Standardized Approach for determining risk weighted assets (RWA).

The increase was primarily driven by net income and a decrease in RWA, partially offset by the payment of common and preferred dividends, as well as common share repurchases and net adverse movements in Accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI).

comparisons.peer_topic: Capital Return and Regulatory Capital Ratios
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm returned $11.80 billion to shareholders via repurchases and dividends in 2024, while maintaining strong regulatory capital positions with a CET1 ratio of 15.0% under Standardized Rules and 15.3% under Advanced Rules as of December 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs reported their CET1 capital ratios for December 2024 under both Standardized and Advanced approaches. JPMorgan reported a Standardized CET1 ratio of 15.7% and an Advanced ratio of 15.8%, while Goldman Sachs reported a Standardized CET1 ratio of 15.0% and an Advanced ratio of 15.3%. JPMorgan's ratios were higher across both measures compared to Goldman Sachs in 2024.
